territories.title: Kingdom of Scotland – politically independent of England
evidence: A separate Scottish king's government, royal seals, judiciary and treaties continued throughout 1500–1509.
Treaty ratified by Henry VII on 1502-10-31 and 1503 dynastic marriage explicitly involved two distinct states; no territorial union.
territories.revenue_note: Do not attribute Scottish taxation to England or UK in 1500–1509.

territories.title: Orkney and Shetland under Scottish Crown with surviving local institutions
evidence: 1468–69 pledged to King James III; king annexed islands 1472-02-20.
Museum research cites Scottish royal governors and tax collectors, while local lawmen and institutions continued.
territories.revenue_note: Tax remittance in 1500–1509 not quantified yet.

territories.title: Western Isles and Highlands – authority contested after Lordship of the Isles forfeiture
territories.legal_actor: Scottish Crown; Clan Donald; regional nobles and clan leadership
evidence: 1493 forfeiture did not imply immediate collapse of Clan Donald influence.
Specialist scholarship finds continuing local power and repeated Crown intervention with regional delegated administration.

geometry.precision: authority and local boundaries not established
geometry.map_rendering: contested / limited royal control, no fully solid shaded Hebrides

territories.title: Treaty of Perpetual Peace 1502
territories.legal_actor: Separate kings Henry VII and James IV
evidence: NRS original signed 1502-10-31 in Westminster SP6/31; 1502 Scottish ratification separately sent to English archives.
1503 dynastic marriage did not merge administrations or control areas.

cautions: Scotland as an independent political actor must not be painted as England in 1500–1509.
Shetland/Orkney not transferred to England by a 1503 royal marriage.
1493 forfeiture of title over Western Isles is not evidence of uniform effective royal governance.
Regional local law autonomy is compatible with Scottish Crown sovereignty; do not treat all law differences as identical political independence.
